sections.heading: C - New York Driver Manual Chapter Ten: Special driving conditions
sections.markdown:
## C - New York Driver Manual Chapter Ten: Special driving conditions

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Special hazards demand sharper attention and judgment across expressways nights weather and emergencies, while grade crossings count as intersections where drivers always expect trains on any track at any time from either side, never race gates or rest on rails, and cross holding lane and gear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=60]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
Active crossings release drivers only after gates fully rise and lamps die since skirting gates or flashing reds is illegal and deadly, passive crossings demand slowed stop-ready approaches with confirmed-clear tracks and all-track both-way scans at multiples, and every visible train runs nearer faster and less stoppable than it looks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=60]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A02
Yellow railroad-cross signs warn crossings ahead demanding caution stop-readiness and care behind stopping buses and trucks, while flashing reds bells or gates command halts at least fifteen feet short with crossings held until silence plus fully raised gates and never ducked around or under moving gates. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=61]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A02
A crossbuck sign requires yielding and shows the number of tracks when multiple exist; you must look and listen and never cross against a near or fast train even if signals fail, never enter unless your vehicle can clear all tracks with room beyond, and expect stops from school buses with or without passengers, passenger-carrying buses, and vehicles carrying explosives or flammable cargo [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=61]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A02
Gateless crossings often paint stop lines to wait behind, and stalled vehicles empty every soul immediately, clear the rails sight-unseen, phone the emergency notification sign, and flee forty-five degrees toward the train since down-track running courts debris. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=61]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A03
Expressways divide one-way multi-lane traffic behind ramp access, post fifty-five normally with sixty-five in rural stretches across thruways interstates and parkways, reward pre-planned entrances and exits, forgive wrong exits only via the next one, and forbid ramp reversing and median crossing as deadly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=62]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A03
Unsigned ramps accelerate to traffic speed for signaled shoulder-checked blends with slowing as needed, stub lanes stop to await wide gaps before sprinting aboard, and cruisers cede the right lane to boarding traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=62]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A03
Lane moves flash signal shoulder-check and cancel, exits pre-read signs claim early lanes signal one hundred feet out and slow to ramp limits, post-exit speedometers re-anchor to slower roads, and fast dense travel demands quicker thinking rest stops and glare-cutting sunglasses. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=62]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A03
Ninety percent of driving decisions ride on sight so nights demand extra caution especially as aging eyes dim, prudent drivers slow below daylight pace on strange or twisting roads, and three-hundred-fifty-foot beams bound safe speed to stopping inside their range. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=62]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A04
Headlight law spans half-hour after sunset to half-hour before sunrise plus sub-thousand-foot visibility and wiper weather, dawn dusk and fog always warrant beams for conspicuity over sight, parking and daytime lamps never substitute, and being flashed means switching on. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=63]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A04
Beams drop within five hundred feet of oncoming traffic and two hundred behind leaders in any lane plus for approaching walkers with aimed auxiliary lamps, un-dimmed meeters earn a one-second high flash before eyes swing right to edge guides, followers dim via night mirrors, and cabins kill roof light dim dashes visor up and clean glass. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=63]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A04
Wet roads including leaf-slicked ones demand slower wider-spaced driving with curve and ramp care, while hydroplaning floats tires off pavement into total traction and steering loss at speed or on worn soft rubber, punishing haste and rewarding deep tread and deeper slowing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=63]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A04
Wiper weather legally mandates true headlights with daytime runners disqualified, low beams pierce falling rain fog and snow that high beams bounce back, signals and braking telegraph earlier, and approved fog lamps run amber-or-white ahead and oversized red astern until clearing skies silence them. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=63]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A05
Winter prep means sound vehicles early snow tires never mixing radial and bias rubber plus studs only October sixteenth through April thirtieth, storms ground all but the compelled who clear every lamp wiper panel and pane with freeze-proof wash, traffic speed rules, and rear-drive slides telegraph while front and all-wheel grip lulls before surprising. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=64]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A05
Rear skids steer the travel direction chasing oscillations while anti-lock brakes press steadily and plain brakes pump quickening with slowing and never stomp, front skids lift gas shift neutral or clutch skip steering until sideways drag restores grip then steer drive and feather gas, prevention brakes early gentle pressed rolling eased and downshifted, and bridges ramps and overpasses freeze first amid lingering slicks. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=64]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A06
Two-thirds of deer strikes land October through December on breeding travel peaking at dawn and dusk against commuter rushes, herds follow leaders, and signed zones mark heavy-hit ground [A06] [A05].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=65]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A06
Deer defense stays alert at dim hours and breeding months, slows near roadsides and crossings expecting bolted followers, flashes warnings to others, and honors posted zones, while every emergency starts by refusing panic across a thinking second or two. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=65]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A06
Blowouts telegraph thumps before demanding death-grip gas-easing ice-skid handling braking-only-when-tame and exits-when-safe with wheel loss echoing plus stop-and-inspect, and steering failure coasts gas-off flashers-on brake-off on straight momentum before feathered stopping. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=65]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A06
Floor-bound brake pedals invite pumping then gradual emergency plus downshift drag, dead headlights try emergency parking and signal lamps for exit light while dimming orders service or stop-and-help, and stuck throttles take shoe-hooks else neutral brake and exit without ever killing ignition into steering lock. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=65]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A06
Pavement departures forbid snap-backs in favor of eased gas gentle braking rear checks and careful returns, and head-on intruders demand slowed rightward horn-blowing refuge never leftward where recovery turns fatal. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=65]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A07
Track stalls under trains shed belts riders and distance toward the train side, then sure-clear windows listen for restarts else neutral shoves clear, while dunkings exploit brief floating for belt-off window exits never doors and sunk cars offer back-seat air pockets for breathed window escapes exhaling upward freely. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=66]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A07
Hood smoke orders off-road parking ignition-off distance and fire-department calls with no heroics, blocked vision borrows side windows flashers and pull-off parking, and the chapter closes quizzing missed exits ramp purpose stub entries exit signaling post-exit checks expressway difference night difficulty beam range blinding beams weather beams skid steering slick braking emergency prime blowouts brake-first moves and pavement returns. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=66]
